meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have until then. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start there.

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. Now tell me on what basis you entered it, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before you did.
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Then show me. And if it's a percentage from a piece of software, save us both the time.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.

Turn the screen toward me, Hale. I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58, Wednesday, October 28. Words appearing in one edit tells you where they were pasted from, not who wrote them, so what else do you have?
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.
In that one file, Hale. Kids write in notebooks and other documents, and you'd know where his drafts are if you'd asked him before you entered the mark. Did you ask him?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.

I'm writing down October 15 and "epistemological paralysis." Students change their argument after an outline, and you still haven't told me whether you spoke to Owen. Whatever happens, Hale, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.
I'll search it tonight, and I'm writing down the line exactly. A bad quotation is a bad quotation, Hale, not a confession. What is it you want from him?
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
Good, because he isn't one. You've shown me documents, Hale, so now show me terms. Whatever they are, nothing goes on his record and nobody in his class hears a word of it.
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.
Hand it over, I'll read both. Tell me what you think I'm looking at, Hale, and then tell me what you're proposing.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

Section 4.4, and I'll hold you to it: private, supervised, not in front of his class, and the zero comes out of the gradebook the moment it's done. I'll agree to that to put this behind him, Hale. I want "nothing goes on his record" in an email from you tonight, with the date and time of the rewrite.
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.
Okay. Which day, Hale, because it has to be marked well before December 1. Put the day, the room and those words about his record in tonight's email, and I'll make sure he's there.
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?
I've told you what I need, Hale. The day, the room, and "nothing goes on his record," in an email tonight, and the zero gone once he's written it.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
Then I'll be watching for it tonight. You still haven't given me a day for the rewrite, Hale, and I have about ten minutes.
Is there anything else you want me to include?
Only what you've already agreed: the day, your room at lunch, "nothing goes on his record," and the zero coming out once he's written it. That's it, Hale.
Then I'll send it by eight.
I'm writing down eight o'clock. The day for the rewrite is still the one thing you haven't given me, Hale.
Thank you for coming in.
I'm still sitting here, Hale. Give me the day for the rewrite, and then I'll go.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Okay, tomorrow, Wednesday, November 11, at lunch in your room, private, the zero out once he's written it, and "nothing goes on his record" in your email by eight tonight.
